outcome: Since 26 January 2024 I found no event bearing on this bullet: no paper, announcement or proof claim treats the convex greedy embedding conjecture for polyhedral graphs as settled. The only in-window item found (Bekos, Da Lozzo, Frati, Liotta and Symvonis, arXiv 2508.19913, 27 August 2025) concerns convex drawings of outerplanar graphs and does not discuss greedy drawing. The most recent substantive work on the convex version (Da Lozzo, D'Angelo and Frati, arXiv 2003.00556, March 2020) treats it as open. A 2009 claim of a probabilistic existence proof (Berchenko and Teicher, PDCAT 2009) is recorded as a pre-window event; I could not read its full text, and no later source I read cites or rebuts it.
problem_asks: One universal existence claim, read from the bullet's wording alone. (1) Quantifier: for every polyhedral graph G, meaning a finite 3-vertex-connected planar graph (by Steinitz's theorem, the skeleton of a convex 3-polytope). (2) For each such G, a convex greedy embedding of G exists. The bullet uses two terms it does not define. 'Greedy embedding': for every ordered pair of distinct vertices s, t, some neighbour of s is strictly closer to t in the target metric. 'Convex': the faces are convex polygons. The bullet does not say (a) that the embedding is planar, (b) that the target is the Euclidean plane, or (c) whether the outer face must also be convex. The Wikipedia article's gloss and the literature (Papadimitriou and Ratajczak, 2005; Da Lozzo, D'Angelo and Frati, 2016) read it as planar, Euclidean, with all faces convex, including the outer face per some sources. Points (a) to (c) are the readings the judging pass must carry; the bullet itself is silent on them. The weak Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture (every 3-connected planar graph has a greedy embedding) is a separate bullet and is not asked here.

events.what_happened: Christos Papadimitriou and David Ratajczak posed the greedy and convex greedy embedding conjectures. Da Lozzo, D'Angelo and Frati's 2016 abstract dates the posing to 2004; the journal publication is 'On a conjecture related to geometric routing', Theoretical Computer Science 344(1), 3–14 (2005), DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2005.06.022 (citation from the Wikipedia article's reference list; the TCS paper was not opened). This is the origin of the problem, not a result on it. Per search snippets, the paper also shows that some graphs (a K(r,6r+1)-type family) admit no greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane.
events.revisions: Journal version 2005 (TCS 344(1)). I did not check whether a 2004 technical report exists.
events.delivers: None on the problem. It states the conjectures and gives non-embeddable examples for the weak form.
events.direction: Origin of the conjecture; no direction on its truth.

events.what_happened: Dhandapani, greedy drawings of triangulations, SODA 2008 (not opened; described in the 2010 Angelini, Frati and Grilli paper and in the small-area survey arXiv 1410.1006, both read only as search snippets). Shows that every planar triangulation has a Euclidean greedy drawing, by a probabilistic argument: a random Schnyder drawing of each triangulation is greedy with positive probability, using the Knaster–Kuratowski–Mazurkiewicz theorem. Existence only, no algorithm.
events.delivers: Existence of Euclidean greedy drawings for planar triangulations only. Whether the drawings are planar with convex faces is not stated in the snippets I read. Schnyder drawings of triangulations have triangular faces, so this may already give the convex version for triangulations (my inference, not checked against the paper).
events.remains: Every polyhedral graph that is not a triangulation. Any constructive or polynomial-time version. Confirmation of convexity, if the triangulation reading is to count as a restricted case.

events.doubts: Probabilistic existence argument, read from a survey snippet. I did not read the SODA paper, so the convexity and planarity of its drawings are not established by me.
events.direction: Cuts for the weak conjecture on triangulations. For the strong conjecture it cuts for it on triangulations only if the drawings are convex, which I did not confirm.
events.object: Not an explicit object. An existence proof: for each triangulation, a random Schnyder drawing is greedy with positive probability (survey snippet).

events.what_happened: Michael T. Goodrich and Darren Strash, 'Succinct Greedy Geometric Routing in the Euclidean Plane' (arXiv 0812.3893; v1 19 December 2008; the version read is v3, last revised 2 October 2009). Abstract, as read on the arXiv page: greedy geometric routing schemes exist for the Euclidean metric in R², for 3-connected planar graphs, with coordinates of O(log n) bits. The abstract does not mention planarity or convexity of the drawing, and does not mention the Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture.
events.revisions: v3 2 October 2009 (per arXiv page); v1 19 December 2008 is the first public version.
events.delivers: Euclidean greedy embedding of every 3-connected planar graph in R², with succinct O(log n)-bit coordinates. Greedy only; not stated to be planar or convex.
events.remains: Convexity of the faces; planarity of the embedding (not claimed); the whole strong conjecture.
events.doubts: None found. The result is not claimed to be planar or convex, so it does not reach the bullet's wording as the literature reads it.
events.direction: Cuts for the weak conjecture (every 3-connected planar graph has a Euclidean greedy embedding), with succinct coordinates. Silent on convexity.

events.what_happened: Tom Leighton and Ankur Moitra, 'Some results on greedy embeddings in metric spaces' (FOCS 2008; Discrete & Computational Geometry 44(3), 686–705, 2010, DOI 10.1007/s00454-009-9227-6 per the Wikipedia article). Settles the Papadimitriou–Ratajczak greedy embedding conjecture: every 3-connected planar graph has a greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane, and so every 3-connected K(3,3)-minor-free graph does. Their embeddings need not be planar (Wikipedia's article; Ghosh and Sinha 2009). Author's manuscript at MIT DSpace handle 1721.1/80843 (abstract read via a search snippet; the MIT PDF was binary to my tool and was not read).
events.revisions: Journal version DCG 44(3), 2010, per the Wikipedia article and the DSpace record.
events.delivers: Euclidean greedy embedding of every 3-connected planar graph. No planarity and no convexity are claimed. Also a combinatorial condition that rules out Euclidean greedy embeddings.
events.remains: Planarity of the embedding and convexity of the faces, that is, the whole strong conjecture. The Wikipedia article and Ghosh and Sinha (2009) both state that the planar convex case is not covered.

checked_by.what_they_did: Independently obtained the same weak result (JGAA 2010, per a search snippet)

events.time_since_posted: not applicable; accepted and widely cited

events.direction: Cuts for the weak conjecture. For the strong conjecture it gives a greedy embedding without planarity or convexity, so it does not settle it.
events.object: Obstructions: a combinatorial condition excluding Euclidean greedy embeddings, and graphs with a greedy embedding but no spanning tree that admits one (search snippets). None concerns convex or polyhedral graphs.

events.what_happened: Patrizio Angelini, Fabrizio Frati and Luca Grilli, 'An algorithm to construct greedy drawings of triangulations' (a GD 2008 paper per a JGAA special-issue note; Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications 14(1), 19–51, 2010). Gives an algorithm that constructs a greedy drawing of any triangulation, via triangulated binary cactuses. The authors state that their techniques extend toward every 3-connected planar graph, and that this was independently shown by Leighton and Moitra. Read as a search snippet; the JGAA paper was not opened.

events.what_happened: Subhas Kumar Ghosh and Koushik Sinha, 'Some results on convex greedy embedding conjecture for 3-connected planar graphs' (arXiv 0905.3812, submitted 23 May 2009; a short version accepted at FCT 2009 per the arXiv comments). Abstract, as read: a planar convex greedy embedding exists exactly when, in the embedding, the ratio of maximum-weight to minimum-weight spanning trees is at most (|V|−1)^(1−δ) for some 0 < δ ≤ 1. They also define a β-weak notion (distance off by a factor β) and show that every 3-connected planar graph has a β-weak planar convex embedding in the Euclidean plane, for a constant β in a stated range (the range is cut off in the text I read). They say they 'make some progress' and do not claim the conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; short version at FCT 2009.
events.delivers: A characterisation of planar convex greedy embeddings through spanning-tree weights, and a β-weak planar convex embedding of every 3-connected planar graph. Neither is an exact convex greedy embedding.
events.remains: An exact (non-weak) convex greedy embedding for all polyhedral graphs, which is the strong conjecture as stated.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted a short version (per the arXiv comments field)

events.doubts: Partial result only; the authors claim progress, not resolution.

The repository abstract (read on the Ben-Gurion CRIS page; the IEEE record returned no content to my tool) says the authors consider the planar convex greedy embedding conjecture and 'give a probabilistic proof for the existence of such embeddings', and discuss a second proof that is almost immediate for embeddings into the 3-sphere. The abstract does not state, as read, whether the class is all 3-connected planar graphs. The sister paper (next event) does say so.

events.what_happened: Yakir Berchenko and Mina Teicher, 'Greedy convex embeddings for sensor networks', PDCAT 2009 (8–11 December 2009), pp. 402–407, DOI 10.1109/pdcat.2009.86. The repository abstract (read on the Bar-Ilan CRIS page) says the authors give 'a random algorithm for embedding 3-connected planar graphs a greedy convex embedding', and that the convex embedding suits sensor networks because each sensor is placed at the midpoint of its neighbours. That midpoint rule resembles a Tutte-type barycentric layout, which is known to give convex faces for 3-connected planar graphs; I did not check whether the paper uses it. The IEEE record returned no content to my tool.

events.what_happened: He and Zhang (names as given in Wang and He's abstract), 'Succinct convex greedy drawing of 3-connected plane graphs', SODA 2011 (not opened; known from a UC Irvine theory-seminar abstract dated November 2010 and from the 2010 small-area survey, both read as search snippets). Per those snippets: the classical Schnyder drawing of a 3-connected plane graph is planar, convex and succinct (integer coordinates in 0 to f, f the number of internal faces), and weakly greedy for a metric H with D ≤ H ≤ 2√2·D, where D is the Euclidean distance.
events.revisions: A November 2010 seminar announced the result; the SODA 2011 date is the proceedings year. The first written version may be earlier; not established.
events.delivers: Planar, convex, succinct drawings of every 3-connected plane graph, greedy only for the modified metric H, not for the Euclidean distance.
events.remains: The Euclidean greedy property, and so the strong conjecture as the literature reads it.

events.what_happened: Jiun-Jie Wang and Xin He, 'Succinct strictly convex greedy drawing of 3-connected plane graphs', Frontiers in Algorithmics and Algorithmic Aspects in Information and Management (Springer LNCS, 2012), DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-29700-7_2. Abstract, as read on Springer Professional (full text paywalled): every 3-connected plane graph has a drawing in R² that is succinct, planar, strictly convex, and greedy with respect to a metric function based on parameters derived from a Schnyder wood. The abstract also says Leighton and Moitra's drawings are not necessarily planar and need Ω(n log n) bits.

events.what_happened: Pierre Leone and Kasun Samarasinghe, 'Every Schnyder drawing is a greedy embedding' (arXiv 1609.04173, one version, submitted 14 September 2016). Abstract, as read on the arXiv page: every Schnyder drawing, a classical way to draw planar graphs, is a greedy embedding 'based on a generalized definition of greedy routing'. The page refers to planar graphs in general. A search snippet gives the arXiv keywords as including 'Maximal planar graphs', and a journal version in Theoretical Computer Science 807 (2019/2020, DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2019.07.021, not opened); the snippet's journal author list has a third author the arXiv version lacks.
events.revisions: arXiv: one version. Journal version in TCS 807 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: Every Schnyder drawing of a planar graph is a greedy embedding under a generalized notion of greedy routing that the abstract does not define. If that notion is the Euclidean one, this gives Schnyder-type greedy embeddings for planar graphs. Whether the drawings are planar with convex faces is not stated in what I read.
events.remains: Which metric the generalized greedy notion uses. If it is not the Euclidean one, the Euclidean convex conjecture is untouched. Convexity of the faces for polyhedral graphs; the keywords suggest the result may be restricted to triangulations, which would leave other polyhedral graphs open.

events.what_happened: Martin Nöllenburg, Roman Prutkin and Ignaz Rutter, 'On self-approaching and increasing-chord drawings of 3-connected planar graphs' (arXiv 1409.0315, v1 1 September 2014; v2 4 December 2014, the full version of a Graph Drawing 2014 paper; Journal of Computational Geometry 7(1), 2016 per a DOAJ listing snippet). Abstract, as read on the arXiv page: triangulations admit increasing-chord drawings in the Euclidean plane (and self-approaching drawings are greedy); planar 3-trees can be drawn planar; 3-connected planar graphs admit increasing-chord drawings in the hyperbolic plane; a binary cactus has no self-approaching drawing. The abstract page does not mention the Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture. A search summary of the paper says it lists whether every 3-connected planar graph has a planar convex Euclidean greedy embedding among its open questions; I did not see that sentence in the text I read.
events.revisions: v2 4 December 2014 (full version of the GD 2014 paper).
events.delivers: Restricted results: increasing-chord (hence greedy) Euclidean drawings for triangulations; planar drawings of planar 3-trees; a hyperbolic result for 3-connected planar graphs. None is a convex Euclidean greedy embedding of all polyhedral graphs.
events.remains: The Euclidean convex conjecture for all polyhedral graphs; per the search summary, the authors list it as open.

events.what_happened: Giordano Da Lozzo, Anthony D'Angelo and Fabrizio Frati, 'On planar greedy drawings of 3-connected planar graphs' (arXiv 1612.09277, v1 29 December 2016, v2 2 January 2017; SoCG 2017, LIPIcs, pp. 33:1–33:16; Discrete & Computational Geometry 63(1), 114–157, 2020, DOI 10.1007/s00454-018-0001-5 per a university repository record, not opened). Abstract, as read on the arXiv page: every 3-connected planar graph admits a planar greedy drawing. The authors call this a 'natural intermediate step towards a proof of the convex greedy embedding conjecture'. The abstract recalls that Papadimitriou and Ratajczak posed the greedy and convex greedy conjectures, and that Leighton and Moitra proved the first.

Bekos, Walter Didimo, Luca Grilli, Philipp Kindermann, Tamara Mchedlidze, Roman Prutkin, Antonios Symvonis and Alessandra Tappini, 'Greedy rectilinear drawings' (arXiv 1808.09063, v1 27 August 2018; v2 11 March 2019; v3 6 August 2019; GD 2018; Theoretical Computer Science 795 (2019), pp. 375–397, per a dblp snippet). events.what_happened: Giordano Da Lozzo, Anthony D'Angelo and Fabrizio Frati, 'On the area requirements of planar greedy drawings of triconnected planar graphs' (arXiv 2003.00556, v1 1 March 2020, v2 3 March 2020; GD 2020, LNCS, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-58150-3_35 per a search snippet). Abstract, as read on the arXiv page: challenges Cao, Strelzoff and Sun's claim that a family of subdivisions of triconnected plane graphs needs exponential area for every planar greedy drawing respecting the embedding. Shows that every n-vertex graph in that family has such a drawing on an O(n)×O(n) grid. Shows that every n-vertex Halin graph has a planar greedy drawing on an O(n)×O(n) grid. Both are obtained by constructing convex, angle-monotone drawings. Also shows that some planar triangulations need exponential area for α-Schnyder drawings with fixed α < 60°. The abstract page does not mention the convex greedy conjecture; the text says the polynomial-area question for triconnected planar graphs is reopened. The Cao, Strelzoff and Sun paper was not located.
events.delivers: Polynomial-grid planar Euclidean greedy drawings for two classes: (a) the Cao–Strelzoff–Sun family of subdivisions, which are not stated to be polyhedral; (b) every Halin graph, which are polyhedral. The Halin drawings are described as convex and angle-monotone. If every face is convex and the greedy property is Euclidean (I took angle-monotone to imply greedy), this settles the strong conjecture for Halin graphs. I did not verify the convexity of all faces from the text. For the general class it settles only area, not existence with convexity.
events.remains: The strong conjecture for all polyhedral graphs outside the Halin class. The polynomial-area question for general triconnected planar graphs, which the paper reopens.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for GD 2020 (per a search snippet)

events.direction: Cuts for the strong conjecture on Halin graphs, if the convexity and greedy readings hold. Otherwise an area result that leaves the convex existence question open.
events.object: Constructions, not counterexamples: a planar greedy grid drawing of each n-vertex Halin graph, built from convex angle-monotone drawings, and of each graph in the Cao–Strelzoff–Sun family. Explicit constructions, not inspected by me.

Bekos, Giordano Da Lozzo, Fabrizio Frati, Giuseppe Liotta and Antonios Symvonis, 'Internally-convex drawings of outerplanar graphs in small area' (arXiv 2508.19913, submitted 27 August 2025; GD 2025, LIPIcs vol. 357). disputes.summary: Leighton and Moitra (FOCS 2008) and Angelini, Frati and Grilli (GD 2008 / JGAA 2010) independently settled the weak greedy conjecture. The sources describe the two as independent and I found no priority dispute.

Berchenko and Teicher (PDCAT 2009, two papers) claim a probabilistic existence proof of planar convex greedy embeddings for 3-connected planar graphs. Later sources I read (Wikipedia's current article, Da Lozzo, D'Angelo and Frati 2016/2017, Nöllenburg, Prutkin and Rutter 2014, Wang and He 2012) treat the convex conjecture as open and do not cite or rebut the claim in the text I read. This is a conflict about status, not a priority dispute, and I have not picked a side.

summary: The bullet is the strong form of the Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture: every polyhedral graph has a convex greedy embedding. The current Wikipedia 'List of unsolved problems in mathematics' lists it under Graph theory, in the Graph drawing and embedding subsection (I read this in the current page; I did not check the 26 January 2024 revision). The weak form (every 3-connected planar graph has a greedy embedding in the Euclidean plane) was settled by Leighton and Moitra in 2008, and independently by Angelini, Frati and Grilli. Neither result gives planarity or convexity. The planar form (every 3-connected planar graph has a planar greedy drawing) was proved by Da Lozzo, D'Angelo and Frati in December 2016, and they present the convex form as still open. Their 2020 area paper reopens a polynomial-area question. It also gives planar greedy grid drawings of every Halin graph, described as convex and angle-monotone, which if the convexity and Euclidean readings hold settles the strong conjecture for that restricted class. I did not confirm that reading from the text. Restricted results on triangulations are pre-window (Dhandapani 2008, existence only, probabilistic; Leone and Samarasinghe 2016, Schnyder drawings are greedy under a 'generalized' greedy notion the abstract does not define, and the keywords suggest triangulations). Results on other metrics or weaker notions are not the Euclidean statement: He and Zhang (2011), Wang and He (2012, strictly convex and greedy for a Schnyder-derived metric), and Ghosh and Sinha (2009, β-weak). The contested item is Berchenko and Teicher, two PDCAT 2009 papers whose repository abstracts claim a probabilistic proof of existence of planar convex greedy embeddings for 3-connected planar graphs. If that holds, the full conjecture was settled before the window. I could not read either full text (the IEEE record returned no content), and none of the later sources I read cites or rebuts them, so I record them as events and not as a verdict. Close calls: (i) whether Berchenko and Teicher's claim covers the full class, which the ad-hoc abstract does not say, though the sensor-network abstract does; (ii) whether the Halin (2020) and triangulation (2008, 2016) results count as restricted cases of the bullet; (iii) whether the bullet's silence on the metric means the Euclidean reading (the literature's) or any metric. Since 26 January 2024 I found no event that bears on the bullet. The in-window item found (Bekos et al., 2025) is about outerplanar graphs and does not mention greedy drawing. AI search: no source I found credits an AI system with work on this bullet. The 2026 AI claims I came across (OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra on the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture; a disputed GPT-5.6 Pro counterexample to Dinitz–Garg–Goemans; a Devin agent's Graffiti-conjecture work; an OpenAI model's disproof of an Erdős unit-distance conjecture) concern other problems. I did not verify them; they come from news or aggregator sources. I did not read Lean or formalisation sources for this bullet; I found none.
competing_reading: The Berchenko–Teicher claim is a 2009 existence proof for the full 3-connected planar class, so the strong conjecture was settled before the window and the later literature's silence is the error. On that reading the problem is solved pre-window and the in-window count is zero. A second reading counts the restricted results as partial resolutions: Dhandapani and Leone–Samarasinghe for triangulations, and the 2020 Halin result for Halin graphs, so the bullet is partly settled by classes. A third reading takes the bullet's silence on the metric literally: then Wang and He (2012), which gives a planar strictly convex greedy drawing of every 3-connected plane graph for a Schnyder-derived metric, settles the bullet pre-window. Against all three, the literature frames the bullet as Euclidean with planar convex faces, and the sources that say so are the Wikipedia article and the 2016 to 2020 papers.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Berchenko and Teicher, PDCAT 2009 (both papers): the scope (3-connected planar graphs, or a subclass), whether the embeddings are planar, convex and Euclidean, and whether the probabilistic argument is complete. (2) Every citation of those two papers after 2009, and any review, erratum or retraction, via Google Scholar's cited-by list or DBLP. (3) The full text of Leone and Samarasinghe (2016), for the generalised greedy notion and the graph class, and of Dhandapani (SODA 2008), for convexity of the triangulation drawings. (4) The full text of Da Lozzo, D'Angelo and Frati (2020, arXiv 2003.00556), for whether every face of the Halin drawings is convex and the greedy property is Euclidean. (5) The 26 January 2024 Wikipedia revision, to confirm the bullet's wording at the freeze. (6) A citing-paper search for 2024 to 2026 on the Da Lozzo et al. papers, which would show whether any in-window result addresses the convex question; my searches found none, but they are not a full index search.
